context.full_target: Let n≥0 be an integer and let E⊆ℝ^n be nonempty and compact. Put I=[0,1] and identify ℝ^n×ℝ with ℝ^{n+1}, using the Euclidean metric. Prove dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, including n=0. Hausdorff measure is the unnormalized countable-diameter-cover measure specified below and dim_H(∅)=0.

record.type: subset of Euclidean ℝ^{n+1}, identified with ℝ^n×ℝ
record.definition: F=E×I. Under the coordinate identification (x,t)↔(x_1,…,x_n,t), the distance between (x,t) and (y,u) is sqrt(‖x-y‖₂²+|t-u|²). For n=0, ℝ^0 consists of its unique empty coordinate vector.

record.type: operator on a metric space X, a positive real s, a positive real δ and a subset A⊆X, valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: For a metric space X, s>0, δ>0 and A⊆X, Hscale(s,δ,A)=inf{Σ_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^s : A⊆⋃_{i≥0}U_i and diam U_i≤δ for every i}. Covers are countable (finite covers are padded by empty sets). The diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances, with diameter of the empty set zero and unbounded diameter +∞; an empty member contributes zero. Sums, infima and suprema are in [0,∞], with inf ∅=∞. Covers are not required to be measurable.

record.type: operator on positive real exponents and subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: For s>0 and a subset A of a metric space X, Hmeasure(s,A)=sup_{δ>0}Hscale(s,δ,A). This is precisely the unnormalized Hausdorff measure convention in problem.md:34-42.

record.type: operator on a real exponent a and a subset A of an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure, valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: Hnative(a,A) denotes the native value (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a)(A) on X. Its full covering formula is sup_{r∈(0,∞]} inf_{T:ℕ→Set X, A⊆⋃_i T_i, ∀i ediam(T_i)≤r} Σ_i w_a(T_i), where w_a(T)=0 for T empty and w_a(T)=(ediam T)^a otherwise; all diameters and operations here are extended nonnegative real operations, including extended real powers. Thus empty sets are zero even at exponent zero. The native definition is the Borel measure Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^a). For ordinary metric spaces ediam is the extended-valued supremum of ordinary distances.

record.type: operator on subsets of extended metric spaces, valued in [0,∞]
record.definition: For A⊆X, hdim(A)=sup{a∈[0,∞):Hnative(a,A)=∞}, with the empty supremum equal to zero and real exponents embedded into [0,∞]. This is the native dimH definition (the exponent is represented by a nonnegative real). It is the usual Hausdorff dimension; in particular the definition assigns zero to the empty set.
D=hdim(E). Once finiteness is proved, real arithmetic with D means its unique finite real representative; no finiteness is assumed by this definition.

record.statement: For every extended metric space X with a measurable space structure equal to its Borel structure, every real a and every A⊆X, Hnative(a,A)=sup_{r∈[0,∞], r>0} inf_{T:ℕ→Set X, A⊆⋃_i T_i, ∀i ediam(T_i)≤r} Σ_i sup_{h:T_i.Nonempty}(ediam(T_i))^a. The inner supremum is zero for an empty T_i and is the indicated power otherwise.

record.statement: For every metric space X, every A⊆X and every real s>0, Hmeasure(s,A)=Hnative(s,A). Moreover Hmeasure(s,A)=0 if hdim(A)<s; Hmeasure(s,A)=∞ if s<hdim(A); Hmeasure(s,A)=0 implies hdim(A)≤s; and Hmeasure(s,A)=∞ implies s≤hdim(A).
